issues.failure_explanation: In the hierarchical block computation two intermediate identities are false as written. (i) Since w_1 contains the moment term -(1/2) sum_i alpha_i^2/(2i+1), the SWE block jump(w)^T f^EC,SWE - avg(w^T B^SWE) jump(u) equals -(1/2) avg(hu_m) sum_i jump(alpha_i^2)/(2i+1), not 0 as claimed in eq:entropy_conservation_condition_swe. (ii) Since the moment component of bar f^EC,SWE is avg(hu_m)avg(alpha_i) + avg(h alpha_i)avg(u_m), the quantity jump(w)^T bar f^EC,SWE - avg(w^T bar B^SWE) jump(u) contains the additional term sum_j jump(alpha_j) avg(hu_m) avg(alpha_j)/(2j+1), which eq:leftside:EC:P drops. Counterexample (N=1, g=1, b=0, (h,u_m,alpha_1)^-=(1,0.3,0.1), (h,u_m,alpha_1)^+=(2,0.7,0.4)): the SWE block equals -0.02125 (not 0) and the bar f^EC,SWE block equals 0.094917 while the claimed expression equals 0.073667; the difference 0.02125 is exactly the dropped term. Because jump(alpha_j^2) = 2 avg(alpha_j) jump(alpha_j), the two errors are equal and opposite, so the final entropy condition and the theorem's statement remain correct (verified numerically: both sides of the full condition equal jump(u_m Psi) = 0.073667 in this example).

failure_location.quote: \jump{\bB{w}}^{\rm T} \mbf{\bar{f}}^{\tt EC, SWE} - \avg{\bB{w}^{\rm T} \mbf{\bar{B}}^{\tt SWE}} \jump{\bB{u}} = \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{1}{2j+1}\Big( \jump{u_m}\avg{h\alpha_j}\avg{\alpha_j} + \jump{\alpha_j}\avg{h\alpha_j}\avg{u_m} + \avg{\alpha_j u_m}\jump{h\alpha_j}\Big) = \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{1}{2j+1} \jump{hu_m\alpha_j^2} = \jump{\mathcal{P}^{\tt LM}}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the two block identities keeping the moment contributions: show the SWE block equals -(1/2) avg(hu_m) sum_i jump(alpha_i^2)/(2i+1) and the bar f^EC,SWE block equals jump(u_m Psi) + (1/2) avg(hu_m) sum_i jump(alpha_i^2)/(2i+1); adding them recovers jump(P^LM). This contained algebraic correction preserves the theorem and all downstream results.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:ec_flux asserts two false intermediate identities, so the proof is invalid as written; the theorem's conclusion (the EC flux satisfies the entropy condition) is nonetheless correct, and the ES scheme (eq:es_dgsem) and the well-balancedness Lemma (lemma:well_balancedness) that build on the flux are unaffected once the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Proof of the EC-flux theorem uses two incorrect block identities (the errors cancel, so the theorem survives)
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained but non-routine algebraic recomputation (tracking the moment terms of w_1 and of bar f^EC,SWE through both blocks and showing the two dropped terms cancel); the theorem and all guarantees survive, so there is no major loss, but the proof as written establishes its intermediate steps through invalid calculations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: that for constant bottom topography satisfies the relation $\text{diag}(\bar{\mbf{H}}, 1) \jump{\bB{w}} = \jump{\bB{u}}$

issues.failure_explanation: Computing the Hessian of E as a function of (h, q, m_i) with q = h u_m, m_i = h alpha_i and inverting gives H^{-1} = (1/g)( y y^T + diag(0, gh, 3gh, ..., (2N+1)gh) ) with y = (1, u_m, alpha^T); the first diagonal entry of z must be 0, not 1. For example, g=1, h=2, u_m=0.5, alpha_1=0.3, N=1: the true (1,1) entry of H^{-1} is 1, while the stated formula gives (1+1)/1 = 2. Hence bar H = H^{-1} + (1/g) e_1 e_1^T, the claim that it is the inverse entropy Hessian is false, and the stated relation diag(bar H, 1) jump(w) = jump(u) also fails. The entropy stability of the scheme is unaffected because the dissipation argument requires only positive definiteness of the dissipation matrix, which bar H still satisfies.

failure_location.quote: \bar{\mbf{H}} := \frac{1}{g}\left(\avg{\mbf{y}}\avg{\mbf{y}}^{\rm T} + \text{diag}(\avg{\mbf{z}}) \right), with vectors $\mbf{y} = (1, u_m, \bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})^{\rm T}$ and $\mbf{z} = (1, gh, 3gh, \dots, (2n+1)gh)^{\rm T}$ is the positive definite inverse of the Hessian of the entropy function $\mathbb{E}\big((h, hu_m, h\bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})\big)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the first entry of the vector z from 1 to 0, i.e., z = (0, gh, 3gh, ..., (2N+1)gh), which makes bar H the inverse Hessian as claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that bar H is the inverse entropy Hessian (and the associated jump relation between entropy and conservative variables) is false; the ES scheme's entropy stability guarantee survives because only positive definiteness of the dissipation matrix is used.
issues.title: The ES dissipation matrix is not the inverse entropy Hessian as claimed (first entry of z is wrong)
issues.why_classification: A one-entry correction restores the claimed property, and the entropy stability guarantee of the ES scheme is preserved unchanged since the proof uses only positive definiteness of the dissipation matrix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the unscaled coefficients are $\widetilde{A}_{ijk}\coloneqq A_{ijk}/(2i+1)$ and $\widetilde{B}_{ijk} \coloneqq B_{ijk}/(2i+1)$

issues.failure_explanation: The identity eq:condition holds for the unscaled coefficients tilde A_{ijk} = A_{ijk}/(2i+1) and tilde B_{ijk} = B_{ijk}/(2i+1); solving it for A gives A_{kji} = -(2k+1)/(2i+1) B_{ijk} - B_{kji}, not A_{kji} = -(B_{ijk} + B_{kji}). The stated formula is only correct when i = k. Counterexample with phi_1 = 1-2zeta, phi_2 = 6zeta^2-6zeta+1: for (i,j,k) = (1,1,2), A_{211} = 5 int_0^1 phi_2 phi_1^2 d zeta = 2/3, while B_{112} = 1/5 and B_{211} = -1, so the stated formula yields 4/5 instead of 2/3. Implemented as written, the procedure computes an incorrect A tensor and hence an incorrect moment flux A-frak; the main text's alternative of computing A directly by Legendre-Gauss quadrature is unaffected, and no formal result depends on the formula.

failure_location.quote: it is computationally more efficient to create the $A_{ijk}$ tensor from the already computed $B_{ijk}$ tensor using the relation \eqref{eq:condition}, i.e., ${A}_{kji} = -({B}_{ijk} +{B}_{kji})$, with $i,j,k = 1,\ldots,N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by A_{kji} = -(2k+1)/(2i+1) B_{ijk} - B_{kji}, or compute A_{ijk} directly from its definition by the Legendre-Gauss quadrature already described in the same appendix.
issues.overall_effect: The computational procedure in sec:computeTensors miscomputes A_{ijk} whenever i != k, which would corrupt the SWME flux and any simulation using that shortcut; the theorems and the directly computed tensors are unaffected.
issues.title: Appendix formula computing A from B misses a normalization factor
issues.why_classification: A single-line normalization fix restores correctness; no theorem, guarantee, or rate depends on the wrong formula, and a valid direct computation is already given in the source.
